subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should this PR's `gateway.peers` plus model-facing `gatewayUrl` design become the core cross-gateway session routing contract, or should it wait for a dedicated federation/peer-auth contract?
rationale: The implementation shape changes gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message routing, and credential handling; automation can find defects, but cannot choose the permanent security/product contract.

options.title: Define Peer Contract Before Merge
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define the allowed peer configuration, identity, token scope, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility semantics, then rework the implementation against that contract.

options.title: Narrow To Configured Peers Only
options.body: Allow a smaller core feature that removes raw `gatewayUrl` tool parameters and only routes through explicitly configured, credentialed peers with tests and live proof.

options.title: Move To Federation Tracker
options.body: Close or supersede this PR in favor of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 if maintainers want broader bridge protocol and identity design first.

recommendation.title: Define Peer Contract Before Merge
recommendation.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define the allowed peer configuration, identity, token scope, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility semantics, then rework the implementation against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history trail crosses session tools, gateway URL auth policy, and gateway protocol/session surfaces.
